nodes.label: LLM Wiki
nodes.author: Charles Hoskinson
nodes.rationale: Knowledge is compiled once on ingest and kept current, so synthesis, cross-references, and contradictions already exist before any question is asked — the opposite of query-time RAG, where the model re-derives everything from raw chunks per query.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Wiki Architecture (raw/wiki/schema)
nodes.author: Charles Hoskinson
nodes.rationale: Raw sources stay immutable as the only ground truth, the wiki is fully LLM-owned and derived, and the schema (CLAUDE.md) co-evolves with the user — separating provenance, synthesis, and governance.

nodes.label: PDF Build Pipeline
nodes.author: Charles Hoskinson
nodes.rationale: Pandoc converts Markdown to LaTeX with custom preamble and Lua filter, a Python post-processor patches table headers for dark mode, XeLaTeX compiles in two passes for TOC and cross-references.

nodes.label: Structural AST Extraction
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and free — structural extraction of code avoids LLM token cost entirely.

nodes.label: Post-Commit Rebuild Hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit with no background process, works with any editor; appends to an existing hook rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: Semantic Extraction Cache
nodes.rationale: Avoids re-paying LLM token cost for files already extracted in prior runs.

nodes.label: Graphify Skill
nodes.rationale: Built around the Karpathy /raw workflow: persistent graph survives sessions, an honest audit trail distinguishes found vs invented edges, and community detection surfaces cross-document connections the user would never think to ask about.

nodes.label: Incremental Update (--update)
nodes.rationale: Only re-extracts new/changed files to save tokens and time.

nodes.label: Query Result Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Answers are saved to graphify-out/memory so the next --update extracts each Q&A as a graph node, improving future queries.

nodes.label: Karpathy /raw Folder Workflow
nodes.rationale: Drop anything into one folder — papers, tweets, screenshots, code, notes — and let structure emerge from extraction rather than manual organization.

nodes.label: Parallel Semantic Extraction Subagents
nodes.rationale: Subagent dispatch in a single message is mandated because sequential one-by-one file reading is 5-10x slower.

nodes.label: URL Ingestion (/graphify add)
nodes.rationale: Auto-detects source type (Twitter/X oEmbed, arXiv, PDF, image, webpage) and saves into ./raw with author/contributor attribution before an incremental graph update.

nodes.label: Watch Mode Auto-Rebuild
nodes.rationale: Code-only changes rebuild via AST with no LLM; doc/image changes only flag needs_update because semantic re-extraction costs tokens. Debounce prevents one rebuild per file during agent write waves.

nodes.label: Wiki Frontmatter Schema
nodes.rationale: created/updated are explicit ISO dates because git resets filesystem mtime on checkout — file.ctime cannot be trusted.

nodes.label: Five Wiki Page Types
nodes.rationale: Concepts are atomic (one idea per page — splitting is correct, merging usually wrong), sources and syntheses are deliberately aggregate, entities map one-per-proper-noun; this keeps cross-reference links precise.

nodes.label: ZES Evidence Tiers
nodes.rationale: Optional 0-3 strength annotations for fine-grained epistemic tracking; the core status field remains mandatory.

nodes.label: Marp Slides (Optional)
nodes.rationale: Wikilinks and embeds do not render in Marp, so marp: true is banned on standard page templates and decks live in a separate slides/ directory outside wiki content.

nodes.label: Obsidian Setup
nodes.rationale: Workspace noise is gitignored but app.json/hotkeys/plugin config stay tracked so Obsidian behavior travels with the repo across machines; attachments live in raw/assets/ co-located with immutable sources.

nodes.label: Batch Ingest
nodes.rationale: Opt-in only; per-source confirmation, fresh dedup, and one atomic commit per source are preserved even in a batch.

nodes.label: Ingest Operation
nodes.rationale: The primary knowledge-accretion loop: source read in full before any claim is written (anti-hallucination guarantee), takeaways discussed with the user before writing, and index updates never deferred because index staleness is the top operational risk.

nodes.label: Init Operation
nodes.rationale: Creates structure only — no stub pages, no faux overview thesis, no speculative maps — because fabricating content with no raw/ source to cite violates provenance; git init plus first commit is mandatory as the baseline safety layer.

nodes.label: Lint Fix Loop
nodes.rationale: Prioritized: structural blockers first, then navigation correctness, discoverability, provenance integrity, and only then semantic accuracy (flag-only) and enrichment.

nodes.label: lint.py Mechanical Accelerator
nodes.rationale: Stdlib-only checker for broken links, orphans, missing frontmatter, and unsourced claims; navigation scaffolding files are exempt because they are catalogs, not content pages.

nodes.label: Query Operation
nodes.rationale: Every claim either carries a wikilink citation to a page read this session, is labeled as non-wiki knowledge, or triggers abstention — there is no third option.

nodes.label: Synthesis File-Back
nodes.rationale: A well-evidenced answer is preserved as a first-class synthesis page with a two-level citation chain (synthesis -> concept/entity page -> raw source) and a 'Derived page' marker; it is an ingest-grade write with full commit discipline.

nodes.label: Two-Level Scrape Dedup
nodes.rationale: URL normalization (scheme/www/tracking-param variants share one dedup key) plus content-hash comparison makes re-fetching idempotent — mirrors and variants produce reported skips, not duplicate raw files.

nodes.label: Fetcher Tier Escalation (http/stealth/dynamic)
nodes.rationale: Escalation is narrow and signal-based (HTTP 401/403/429, challenge markers, near-zero extracted text) — not fuzzy guessing; dynamic is the terminal tier and the tier used is recorded in frontmatter.

nodes.label: Scrape/Crawl Operation
nodes.rationale: An optional Claude-Code-only on-ramp: it only prepares raw/ files; the wiki itself is always written by the standard v1 ingest. Crawls always plan first (--plan-only) as a runaway and cost control.

nodes.label: WebFetch Fallback
nodes.rationale: Last-resort single-URL capture when Scrapling is declined or unavailable; output is model-interpreted, so it is stamped is_verbatim: false and may never be quoted verbatim.

nodes.label: llm-wiki Eval Suite
nodes.rationale: Checks that the skill triggers when it should, stays quiet when it shouldn't (negative cases like third-party wikis and ad-hoc notes), and that each operation behaves correctly; re-run after editing descriptions or playbooks.

nodes.label: Edge Confidence Audit Trail (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS)
nodes.rationale: Every edge is tagged so the user knows what was found versus invented; uncertainty is flagged AMBIGUOUS rather than omitted.

nodes.label: Graphify Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge; always show token cost and raw cohesion scores; warn before oversized HTML viz — the graph's value depends on trustworthiness.

nodes.label: Append-Never-Overwrite Contradiction Rule
nodes.rationale: When sources disagree, both positions go in a [!conflict] callout with status: contested; deciding which claim is canonical is a human decision, never Claude's. Supersession (newer authoritative value) is distinct and keeps a dated note of the old value.

nodes.label: Dedup Before Create
nodes.rationale: Three-step search (index.md, category _index.md, aliases) plus filename-equals-canonical-title makes re-ingest idempotent and prevents duplicate pages.

nodes.label: Index Router and MOC Discipline
nodes.rationale: index.md is a router, not a full listing — keeping per-query token cost roughly flat as the wiki grows; MOCs split at ~25-30 entries so any navigational file stays scannable in one pass. Links express aboutness; tags express context/state.

nodes.label: Orphan Prevention Rule
nodes.rationale: Every new page needs one outbound wikilink, one MOC entry, and one category index entry before commit so it stays discoverable in the graph.

nodes.label: Inline Provenance Marker
nodes.rationale: A bare source link without a locator is insufficient (UNSOURCED lint defect); quote anchors written only from the open raw file prevent hallucination drift from prior model memory.

nodes.label: Wikilink-Only Internal Linking
nodes.rationale: Markdown links break Obsidian backlinks, graph view, and Dataview queries; standardizing on [[wikilinks]] keeps all three working. Renames must go through Obsidian or update all referrers in the same commit.

nodes.label: Atomic Ingest Commit
nodes.rationale: One commit per ingest is the unit of undo (git revert), the backup mechanism, and the provenance audit trail; partial state breaks the invariants lint and query depend on. The raw source is committed too so citations are reproducible from the repo alone.

nodes.label: Wiki Discovery Contract
nodes.rationale: A directory is a wiki iff CLAUDE.md's first non-empty line is the '<!-- llm-wiki: v1 -->' marker AND a wiki/ folder exists; walking up from cwd makes every operation auto-discover the wiki without configuration — nothing is hardcoded to a specific repo.

nodes.label: Canonical Prose Semantic Pass
nodes.rationale: The LLM's prose pass is the canonical lint so linting works fully on surfaces without code execution; the script only accelerates the stable mechanical subset and cannot drift from prose conventions.

nodes.label: Query Abstention Behavior
nodes.rationale: 'I don't have enough in the wiki to answer that' is a correct, complete answer — always preferable to a confident answer drawn from model memory; the abstention suggests a concrete source to ingest.

nodes.label: Index-First Read Path
nodes.rationale: Three-level drill-down (root index, category index, page) keeps token cost roughly flat as the wiki grows and guards against answering from a stale or guessed page name.

nodes.label: Parametric Knowledge Labeling
nodes.rationale: Model-memory content must be labeled adjacent and unambiguously ('not from wiki') so the user always knows which parts of an answer are wiki-grounded; the label is not a license to pad answers with model memory.

nodes.label: is_verbatim Provenance Flag
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes byte-derived extraction (quotable verbatim) from model-interpreted WebFetch content (paraphrase only) — preserving the wiki's exact-quote provenance integrity.

nodes.label: Scrape Surface Gate
nodes.rationale: Fetch attempts on the API sandbox or claude.ai fail or hang (no network, no installs), so the gate forces a clean refusal with fallback options instead of retries or browser downloads.

nodes.label: Quantum Shelf Life of Trusted Setups
nodes.norm_label: quantum shelf life of trusted setups

nodes.label: Capex/Opex Setup Economics Framework
nodes.rationale: Author's lens for why trusted setups persist: the ceremony is a one-time capital expenditure amortized across every circuit, while per-proof verification is operating expense -- the argument for ceremonies is economic, not philosophical.

nodes.label: manim_render.py
nodes.rationale: The module owns validation of scene values against the Sage manifest so an animation can never drift from the math.

nodes.label: run_sage.py
nodes.rationale: A recipe must print a one-line JSON values manifest as its last stdout line; the manifest is the source of truth for every numeric or visual claim downstream.

nodes.label: graphify WSL Install
nodes.rationale: graphify is installed from its real git source - the PyPI package graphifyy is a flagged typosquat and must not be used.

nodes.label: Correct-by-Construction Sage Figures
nodes.rationale: Every figure is generated from a Sage computation that emits a values manifest; prose and animation claims are checked against the manifest so numbers can never silently drift from the math.

nodes.label: Sanderson + Tao Method Engine
nodes.rationale: Two reference cards (ten Sanderson moves, Tao's three rigor phases and two maxims) are loaded on every run and act as an enforced rubric, not aspiration - the Stage 6 scorecard checks them.

nodes.label: Method-Adherence Scorecard Gate
nodes.rationale: A failing scorecard returns the bundle to the responsible stage rather than shipping - method adherence becomes testable pass/fail.

nodes.label: No-Fallback Invariant
nodes.rationale: This is a pipeline test: every dependency must be installed, live, and actually invoked; the skill's degraded modes are disabled so a missing dependency aborts the run instead of silently falling back.

nodes.label: Privacy as a Luxury Good
nodes.rationale: The hardware ladder argument: client-side proving (maximum privacy) demands hardware most of the world does not own, so over 90% of people must delegate proving and trust a service with their secrets -- the technical Memory Gap becomes a political equity problem.

nodes.label: BN254 Curve (~100-bit security after Tower NFS)
nodes.norm_label: bn254 curve (~100-bit security after tower nfs)

nodes.label: Cryptographic Primitives Trilemma
nodes.rationale: The author's own framing (explicitly not from the literature): a commitment scheme achieves at most two of algebraic functionality, post-quantum security, and succinctness. Presented as a historical snapshot being actively dissolved by the lattice folding line, not a permanent law.

nodes.label: Verification-Key Binding Failures
nodes.rationale: Real soundness bugs in recursive systems are rarely deep cryptography — they are binding failures; bind VK hashes into statements, domain-separate transcripts, treat every cross-layer interface as adversarial.

nodes.label: Customizable Constraint Systems (CCS)
nodes.rationale: Generalizes R1CS, Plonkish and AIR under one umbrella with higher-degree constraints.

nodes.label: Elliptic Curve Cycles
nodes.rationale: Two curves, each one's scalar field equal to the other's base field, alternating per recursion layer to fix the verifier/circuit field mismatch; finding good cycles remains a hard open problem.

nodes.label: CycleFold
nodes.rationale: The second curve is only needed for a handful of foreign-field group ops, so its circuit shrinks to a single scalar multiplication (~1,500 gates) whose correctness is folded on the primary curve.

nodes.label: Full Recursion
nodes.rationale: Embed the complete inner verifier in-circuit; the field-mismatch problem (base vs scalar field) is classically fixed with a cycle of elliptic curves.

nodes.label: HyperNova
nodes.rationale: Sum-check-based multifolding of CCS keeps verifier work logarithmic as constraint degree grows and avoids committing to cross-term error vectors entirely.

nodes.label: Nova
nodes.rationale: Reference folding construction: the augmented step circuit verifies the previous fold with two group scalar multiplications and a hash (~10^4 constraints vs 10^6+ for an embedded SNARK verifier).

nodes.label: R1CS
nodes.rationale: Naive instances don't fold: the quadratic constraint produces cross terms under random linear combination that satisfy no instance.

nodes.label: Relaxed R1CS
nodes.rationale: Adds scalar u and error vector E (Az . Bz = u*(Cz) + E), shaped exactly to absorb the folding cross terms; relaxation makes the satisfiability set closed under interpolation.

nodes.label: Spartan
nodes.rationale: Final compression SNARK in the Nova reference implementation; sum-check over multilinear extensions with no FFTs pairs naturally with Nova.

nodes.label: SuperNova
nodes.rationale: Non-uniform IVC: one running instance per instruction type selected by a program counter, avoiding the universal switch circuit that would reintroduce the costs folding was meant to kill.

nodes.label: BCTV, Scalable ZK via Cycles of Elliptic Curves (CRYPTO 2014)
nodes.norm_label: bctv, scalable zk via cycles of elliptic curves (crypto 2014)

nodes.label: Nguyen-Boneh-Setty, Revisiting Nova on a Cycle of Curves (ePrint 2023/969)
nodes.norm_label: nguyen-boneh-setty, revisiting nova on a cycle of curves (eprint 2023/969)

nodes.label: draft_lint.py
nodes.rationale: Must report CLEAN: no pipeline/QA vocabulary or machine headings in reader-facing prose.

nodes.label: math-explainer Skill
nodes.rationale: Turns 'explain <concept>' into book-ready material executing the Sanderson + Tao teaching method; the Stage 6 gate must never be skipped so quality is enforced, not asserted.

nodes.label: Tao: There's More to Mathematics than Rigour and Proofs
nodes.norm_label: tao: there's more to mathematics than rigour and proofs

nodes.label: Draft-Quality Rules
nodes.rationale: Scorecard gates method structure; these editorial-panel rules gate reader experience: define load-bearing terms inline, gloss notation at first use, prose over lists, one home per derivation, name both moduli in group crypto, end on a forward beat.

nodes.label: Sanderson Moves
nodes.rationale: Ten intuition-building moves (lead with the visual, concrete before abstract, motivate before defining, invite active rediscovery); the binding constraint is motivation, not polish.

nodes.label: Tao Staging
nodes.rationale: Pre-rigorous -> rigorous -> post-rigorous phases; rigour should destroy bad intuition while elevating good, and every picture is paired with its formal statement.

nodes.label: Six-Stage Explanation Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Scope/deps -> stuck-point prediction -> multimodal explanation -> accuracy verification -> comprehension checks -> assembly & gate; stages run in order and ship only when the scorecard PASSes and the draft lints CLEAN.

nodes.label: Entity Map (entity-map.json)
nodes.rationale: The entity map is authoritative for enrichment so agents cannot hallucinate cross-references; seeded entities plus auto-discovered proper nouns appearing in 4+ sections.

nodes.label: 14 Parallel Chapter Extraction Agents
nodes.rationale: Chapters write to disjoint wiki/sections slices, so a shared workspace is safe; verbatim body preservation makes extraction deterministic and idempotent.

nodes.label: Section Manifest (section-manifest.json)
nodes.rationale: Manifest-driven extraction: the manifest is the authoritative work assignment so 14 parallel agents write disjoint slices with no write conflicts, and failed chapters can be rerun idempotently.

nodes.label: Five Audit Dimensions (Accuracy, Citations, Clarity, Coherence, Depth)
nodes.norm_label: five audit dimensions (accuracy, citations, clarity, coherence, depth)
nodes.rationale: Severity tags P0-P3 keep the audit honest: the improvement loop acts only on P0/P1, so style over-flagging cannot dominate revision.

nodes.label: Chapter-by-Chapter Improvement Loop
nodes.rationale: One chapter per cycle because section-level rewrites risk losing transitions; chapters ordered by P0/P1 finding density.

nodes.label: CONCEPTS_FOR_BOOK.md Coverage Report
nodes.rationale: Concepts ranked by centrality and reference support, each tagged well-covered / under-covered / absent versus the manuscript with a per-chapter rollup - the graph's recommendation engine for the book.

nodes.label: Two-Phase Extraction Strategy
nodes.rationale: Parallel mechanical extraction first, then an enrichment pass with global visibility - extraction is embarrassingly parallel but enrichment needs cross-chapter context (entity map, dependencies, contradictions).

nodes.label: Four Layer-2 Language Philosophies
nodes.rationale: The taxonomy (EVM-compatible, ZK-native ISA, general-purpose ISA, application-specific DSL) is framed around what the developer sees, because what the developer sees determines what bugs they make -- and bugs, not cryptographic breaks, are the largest source of real-world ZK failures.

nodes.label: The Witness Gap (50-70% of proving time)
nodes.norm_label: the witness gap (50-70% of proving time)

nodes.label: Midnight
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the book's full-stack running case study because the author founded IOG, the company that built it, giving access to internal architecture at unusual depth; the author flags the bias and designs Chapter 12's claims to be independently verifiable. Framed as a 'privacy theater' where ZK proofs are the execution model itself, not an optimization.

nodes.label: The Cascade Effect / One-Way Door
nodes.rationale: Layer 6 field choice cascades upward with algebraic necessity -- field determines commitment scheme, which determines proof system, which determines arithmetization -- so 'crypto-agility' is largely fiction for ZK systems; changing the field is a full redesign.

nodes.label: Seven-Layer Model
nodes.rationale: The book's organizing frame: every ZK system decomposes into seven layers (setup, language, witness, arithmetization, proof system, primitives, verification). The author presents it as a pedagogical map that is deliberately provisional -- by Chapter 10 it is redrawn as a DAG with fourteen causal edges because real systems fuse and invert the layer boundaries.

nodes.label: 4x4 Sudoku Running Example
nodes.rationale: Chosen because it is small enough to hold in your head, complex enough to exercise every layer (range checks, uniqueness, boundaries), and needs no math background; it is traced through Chapters 3-6 as program, witness, 72-96 constraints, and sealed proof.

nodes.label: Trust-Minimized (vs Trustless)
nodes.rationale: The book's central thesis: 'trustless' is marketing; ZK proofs do not eliminate trust but decompose one monolithic assumption into seven independent, weaker, testable ones. The author deliberately adopts the uglier word because it is accurate.

nodes.label: Aggregation Trees
nodes.rationale: Tree shape is a tuning knob: deeper trees cut per-node prover cost and parallelize; shallower trees cut latency and total work.

nodes.label: Folding Schemes
nodes.rationale: Reduce checking two instances to one; deliberately weaker than an argument of knowledge because weaker primitives admit simpler, faster realizations. Costs: no standalone mid-computation proof, mandatory additively homomorphic commitments, final compression SNARK required.

nodes.label: Incrementally Verifiable Computation (IVC)
nodes.rationale: Two independence conditions — update work and verify work independent of step count — distinguish IVC from naive prove-the-whole-history approaches.

nodes.label: Proof-Carrying Data (PCD)
nodes.rationale: Generalizes IVC from a chain to a DAG across mutually distrusting parties; IVC is the path-graph special case; compliance predicates define local correctness.

nodes.label: ProtoStar / ProtoGalaxy
nodes.rationale: Folding as a compiler: any special-sound protocol becomes a folding/accumulation scheme, yielding lookups with prover cost independent of table size; ProtoGalaxy folds many instances with sublinear verifier cost.

nodes.label: Recursion Gap
nodes.rationale: The multiplicative overhead of proving a verifier versus just running it; levers include smaller fields, better in-circuit hashes, lookups, and folding's near-elimination of the embedded verifier.

nodes.label: SBOM Verification as PCD
nodes.rationale: A software bill of materials is a dependency DAG, and dependency DAGs are PCD graphs — the outline's canonical real-world PCD instance, with one root proof over the transitive closure.

nodes.label: Succinctness Threshold
nodes.rationale: The verifier circuit must be asymptotically and concretely smaller than the statements proven or recursion diverges; accumulation and folding deliberately relax this by deferring expensive checks.

nodes.label: Verifiable AI (zkML)
nodes.rationale: Neural networks are chains of structurally similar layers — exactly IVC's shape; distinguish proof of inference, model provenance, and training (vastly harder).

nodes.label: Recursive Proof Composition Outline
nodes.rationale: Three-chapter treatment (survey, folding deep dive, applications); historical arc theme: each generation moved more work out of the recursive step.

nodes.label: Compression, Incrementality, Composability
nodes.rationale: Recursion buys three distinct things and conflating them causes confusion; each maps to different applications and constructions.

nodes.label: Book Graph (book-graph/)
nodes.rationale: An independent manuscript-only graph in its own directory never touches graph 1, preserving a clean comparison baseline.

nodes.label: Reference Subgraph Augmentation
nodes.rationale: Reuses graph 1's already-mined reference nodes instead of re-extracting; scrapling re-runs only as an idempotent confirmation of the corpus.

nodes.label: Vocabulary Drift Risk
nodes.rationale: Different concept ids for the same idea would understate overlap; subagents prefer graph 1's existing concept ids and the comparison matches on normalized labels.

nodes.label: Shared concept_<kebab> Node IDs
nodes.rationale: Shared concept ids are how distinct papers interlink on merge - the source of cross-paper surprising connections; imprecise names risk wrongly merging distinct concepts.

nodes.label: Subagent Extraction Contract
nodes.rationale: Fixed prompt: read the full PDF, emit 10-25 nodes (constructions, theorems, assumptions, citations), every node anchored, source_location required, uncertain edges tagged AMBIGUOUS - caps over-generation.

nodes.label: Master Graph (master-graph/)
nodes.rationale: A new directory unifies the three graphs while leaving them untouched as provenance and comparison baselines (augmenting graphify-out in place was rejected).

nodes.label: Per-Chapter Split Extraction
nodes.rationale: A single-file extraction of the 919 KB manuscript extracts shallowly (the same failure dense PDFs showed), so the book is split at chapter headings with one extraction subagent per chapter.

nodes.label: Additive Anchored Extraction
nodes.rationale: Additive so existing chapter-to-paper cross-edges survive; anchored to each paper's existing node ids so new deep nodes attach to the right place in the graph.

nodes.label: merge_fragment Additive Merge
nodes.rationale: Union nodes by id with existing-wins, union edges by (source, target, relation), drop dangling, and assert the additive invariant so a merge can never lose graph content.

nodes.label: Canonical slides.pdf source_file
nodes.rationale: Transcript-derived nodes share slides.pdf as source_file so one lecture cannot double-count as two reference supports; source_location distinguishes slide vs transcript origin.

nodes.label: Dual-Interpreter Discipline
nodes.rationale: The venv (scrapling + youtube-transcript-api) runs fetch and tests; the system Python (graphify + networkx + pypdf) runs merge; lazy imports keep the module importable under the venv.

nodes.label: Slides-PDF-Not-Frames Decision
nodes.rationale: The course publishes clean slide PDFs, so no ffmpeg/OCR/frame extraction is needed; youtube-transcript-api pulls the transcript reliably where raw scrapling of the timedtext endpoint returns an empty body.

nodes.label: build_alias_map Deterministic Dedup
nodes.rationale: Group nodes by normalized label; within a group the highest-degree node is canonical; validation rejects chains and alias-as-canonical before consolidation.

nodes.label: score_concepts Ranking
nodes.rationale: Concepts ranked by degree + 2x reference support, so literature-backed concepts outrank merely well-connected ones.

nodes.label: should_stop Bounded Stop-Check
nodes.rationale: Three limits - 3 rounds, fewer than 10 new relevant papers (convergence), 150-fetch hard cap - enforced on persisted state so a crashed and resumed run cannot exceed them.

nodes.label: Hub LLM Synonym Pass
nodes.rationale: LLM merge proposals are limited to the top-100 hub nodes and persisted to aliases.json for review - bounding cost and guarding against over-merging distinct concepts.

nodes.label: Bounded Citation Snowball
nodes.rationale: Citations are snowballed out of fetched papers but bounded (3 rounds / 10-new convergence / 150 hard cap) because unbounded expansion drifts toward tangential subfields and unbounded spend.

nodes.label: Hybrid Relevance Filter
nodes.rationale: A free lexical prefilter against the graph vocabulary plus a ZK keyword list drops off-topic works before any API spend; the LLM judge sees only survivors.

nodes.label: _CF_SESSIONS Per-Origin Cache
nodes.rationale: Clear an origin at most once per process; failures are not cached so a later entry can retry.

nodes.label: _looks_like_cloudflare Detector
nodes.rationale: Escalation must be specific: only 403s or Cloudflare interstitial markers trigger a browser launch, so a plain 404 never spends one.

nodes.label: cf_clearance Cookie + UA Reuse
nodes.rationale: cf_clearance is bound to the exact user-agent that minted it, so cookie and UA are harvested together and replayed on the curl_cffi download.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Stealth Tier
nodes.rationale: A stealth browser clears the challenge once per origin; curl_cffi then reuses the harvested session so unattended --force reruns and fresh clones succeed without a manual cookie harvest.

nodes.label: Live Verification Results (refs 6/17/45)
nodes.rationale: First run failed (landing-page clearing found no challenge); after the clear-URL fix the PDF-URL clear solved the managed Turnstile, produced a byte-identical 404221-byte PDF, and the origin cache amortized the solve across refs 17 and 45.

nodes.label: ePrint Cloudflare Stealth Tier Design Spec
nodes.norm_label: eprint cloudflare stealth tier design spec

nodes.label: In-Flight Premise Corrections
nodes.rationale: Two plan premises were corrected during execution: StealthyFetcher is Chromium-based and does expose solve_cloudflare (the earlier claim came from a grep that skipped the gitignored .venv), and the clear step must target the challenged PDF URL because eprint's challenge is path-scoped.

nodes.label: Clear the Challenged PDF URL
nodes.rationale: eprint's Cloudflare challenge is scoped to the PDF asset paths; the landing page serves 200 unchallenged and never mints cf_clearance, so solve_cloudflare must run against the failing PDF URL itself.

nodes.label: Debt Ledger Device
nodes.rationale: Every trust-us-proof-comes-later note is named, tracked, and visibly paid on a named page - what lets the book defer rigor without losing reader trust.

nodes.label: IOP + PCS = SNARK Unification
nodes.rationale: Every proof system met so far is the same two-part machine - a polynomial-IOP compiled by a polynomial-commitment scheme; this unification is the book's intellectual summit.

nodes.label: Part III Dependency-Pure Rigorous Engine
nodes.rationale: No chapter uses a tool an earlier one has not built: random evaluation, MLE + Schwartz-Zippel, sum-check/GKR, the IOP + PCS recipe, families derived, the bedrock, Fiat-Shamir/ROM/AGM.

nodes.label: 4x4 Sudoku Running Example
nodes.rationale: Sudoku owns the mechanism and Midnight owns the consequence - a strict division of labor so the two running examples never compete on the same page.

nodes.label: Seven-Layer Trust Decomposition Thesis
nodes.rationale: A ZK proof does not abolish trust - it decomposes one act of faith into seven independently testable, replaceable, breakable bets; the layers are the plot, each introduced under suspicion with its real-world scar.

nodes.label: Single Forward Pass Structure
nodes.rationale: Intuition-first apprenticeship then the rigorous engine at the center: front-loading sum-check/IOP/MLE would lose most readers by page 40, and a two-lap walk would re-walk the layers twice.

nodes.label: Six-Lens Architect Synthesis
nodes.rationale: Six expert architects designed independent outlines against the master graph through different lenses; the narrative-arc skeleton won because it satisfies both the Feynman constraint and the definitive-volume constraint.

nodes.label: scorecard.py
nodes.rationale: Binds accuracy/comprehension checks to embedded artifacts validated by schemas.py so a self-asserted flag cannot pass the gate.

nodes.label: accuracy_report
nodes.rationale: verified must be true before Stage 6; includes manifest_ref, claim_checks, ledger_refs, adversarial_findings.

nodes.label: bundle.json Bundle
nodes.rationale: Evidence-bearing, not self-attested: embeds the Stage-4 accuracy_report and Stage-5 comprehension_set so a bare accuracy_verified flag cannot pass the gate.

nodes.label: comprehension_set
nodes.rationale: Recall/apply/transfer plus a re-derive task; each item targets a Stage-2 stuck-point with an answer key and an on-miss route to a Stage-1 prerequisite.

nodes.label: Correct-by-Construction Figures
nodes.rationale: Every figure comes from a Sage recipe that returns a values manifest; any prose claim not backed by the manifest is recomputed in Sage or removed.

nodes.label: Graphify Best-Effort Enrichment
nodes.rationale: graphify fuzzy-matches labels and can land on homonyms/near-misses; it is enrichment, not a gate — bad matches are recorded honestly (graphify_match) and never worked around with wrong edges.

nodes.label: Kindle EPUB Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Reflowable format per Amazon Kindle Publishing Guidelines v2025.1: MathML for math, HTML tables, custom CSS for Kindle Enhanced Typesetting (kindle.css, kindle-filter.lua, metadata.xml).

nodes.label: Hybrid STARK-to-SNARK Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The dominant 2026 production pattern: a transparent STARK inner proof (no ceremony, post-quantum) recursively compressed and wrapped in Groth16 for cheap on-chain verification. The SNARK-vs-STARK debate was a false dichotomy; Ethereum gas economics forced 'STARK inside, SNARK outside'.

nodes.label: resolve_deps.py
nodes.rationale: Kept as a pure MATH_FOUNDATIONS parser with no graphify import so it runs under the pytest venv (dual-interpreter rule).

nodes.label: LatticeFold
nodes.rationale: Replaces Pedersen with Ajtai-style lattice commitments for post-quantum folding; core obstacle: lattice commitments are homomorphic only for short vectors and random linear combinations destroy shortness.

nodes.label: Pedersen Commitments in Folding
nodes.rationale: Additive homomorphism lets the verifier fold commitments with two scalar multiplications while the prover folds the vectors; this discrete-log dependence is precisely where post-quantum folding gets stuck.

nodes.label: MATH_FOUNDATIONS.md
nodes.rationale: Read-only authoritative dependency source: concept, stratum, first-needed chapter, depth code (I/R/A), prerequisites.

nodes.label: Dual-Interpreter Rule
nodes.rationale: resolve_deps.py stays import-pure to run under the pytest venv; graphify and CHAPTER_BIBLE are read via the project's system Python.

nodes.label: merge_extraction Helper
nodes.rationale: Union nodes by id (first wins), union edges, drop dangling - the shared fragment-merge semantics reused across graph builders.

nodes.label: Concept-Label Jaccard Comparison
nodes.rationale: Comparison normalizes labels (depluralize, strip parentheticals) rather than ids so synonym vocabulary drift between graphs still counts as overlap.

nodes.label: fetch_references --manifest Flag
nodes.rationale: Parameterizing the manifest path lets the hardened fetch pipeline run unchanged on the recursion corpus.

nodes.label: Reuse Entries for 9 Overlap Papers
nodes.rationale: Nine papers already in the main corpus point at existing PDFs and their existing deep fragments, so nothing is re-downloaded or re-extracted.

nodes.label: Recursion Outline (3 Chapters)
nodes.rationale: First step toward adding recursion chapters to the book; writing chapter prose is explicitly out of scope.

nodes.label: Continuations / Sharding
nodes.rationale: The most economically important recursion pattern today: chunk the trace, prove chunks in parallel on GPU clusters, recursively merge with boundary-consistency checks between adjacent chunks.

nodes.label: Fractal
nodes.rationale: First transparent, post-quantum recursion via holography.

nodes.label: Hybrid Proving Pipelines
nodes.rationale: Dominant production pattern: parallel STARK prover for bulk execution, recursive STARK aggregation, final SNARK wrap for cheap on-chain verification — with the uncomfortable tradeoff that the wrapper often reintroduces a trusted setup.

nodes.label: Real-Time L1 Proving
nodes.rationale: Ethereum L1 zkEVM requires block proofs in ~10-12s, proof size under 300 KiB, and no trusted-setup recursive wrappers; the race went from ~200 GPUs (2025) to 16 GPUs (2026).

nodes.label: Rollups and Proof Compression
nodes.rationale: The original killer app: recursion aggregates per-batch proofs and compresses the final proof for cheap on-chain verification (the canonical STARK-to-SNARK squeeze).

nodes.label: STARK Recursion
nodes.rationale: Small fields (Goldilocks, BabyBear, Mersenne-31), algebraic hashes (Poseidon) and lookup arguments made FRI verification in-circuit practical; transparent and plausibly post-quantum.

nodes.label: Batch-1 Checkpoint Gate
nodes.rationale: A 10-paper batch with a delta report gates the remaining ~36 PDFs on explicit user approval before more token spend.

nodes.label: Do Not Run graphify update on the Content Graph
nodes.norm_label: do not run graphify update on the content graph
nodes.rationale: graphify-out is a content graph with explicit excludes; running graphify update from the repo root would pollute it with scripts/tests tooling, and leaving graphify-out/manifest.json untouched keeps a future update from re-extracting and overwriting the deep-mined nodes.

nodes.label: Pilot-Then-Parallel Orchestration
nodes.rationale: Schwartz-Zippel runs in-session first to validate the layout and real Sage/manim/graphify renders, becoming the worked template for four parallel Opus subagents in isolated draft dirs.

nodes.label: Reference Manifest (references/manifest.json)
nodes.rationale: Hand-curated single source of truth for all 63 bibliography refs (ids, chapters, types, URLs, files); ids 34/54 are bibliography gaps and 47/48 are duplicate_of re-listings with no download.

nodes.label: Stub Entries for Print-Only Sources
nodes.rationale: Stubs carry full citation metadata so paywalled or print-only sources still become knowledge-graph nodes.

nodes.label: Two-Tier Scrapling Fetch
nodes.rationale: curl_cffi Fetcher impersonation first, StealthyFetcher headless browser only for blocked or JS-heavy pages - the cheap path is tried before the expensive one.

nodes.label: Graph Corpus: Manuscript + References + Wiki
nodes.rationale: Build artifacts (fonts, TeX, the book's own PDF) must stay out of the graph - exclude support preferred, staged corpus/ directory as fallback.

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph + Reference Corpus Design Spec
nodes.norm_label: knowledge graph + reference corpus design spec

nodes.label: Manifest-Driven Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Bibliography parse ambiguities are resolved during hand curation of the manifest, not silently guessed by the script; the script only executes the manifest.

nodes.label: Extractor Blowup
nodes.rationale: Recursion composes extractors, so knowledge-soundness theorems hold only for constant or logarithmic depth while deployed systems recurse thousands of times.

nodes.label: Fiat-Shamir in IVC

nodes.label: Atomic Accumulation
nodes.rationale: Halo's insight: the expensive MSM check need not run in-circuit each step — fold it into a running accumulator verified once at the end; this removed trusted setup from practical recursion and is the conceptual bridge to folding.
